upstream.scope: Identity-checked, bounded-lifetime Linux process handles for signaling (D1 §§6.2, 27; D2 T32; K1-K3): pidfd_open, then the sampled ProcessKey re-checked against /proc/<pid>/stat after the open; at most 16 handles for at most 30 s, closed on cancellation, expiry, settlement and drop; one closed signal (SIGTERM) sent only through the descriptor; unsupported (not Linux, ENOSYS, a filter's EPERM, ENODEV) and descriptor exhaustion reported, never retried and never answered by a PID-addressed kill. No action path reaches it: the dry-run executor is still the only production executor, and PX-008's audit allows exactly the module's two system calls and refuses any other production reference to it. No protocol, registry, SDK, runtime, renderer or client change. Contributes to HTOP-R1-001 (owner PX-028/PX-031), which stays planned until PX-030 and PX-031 deliver a real, observed action

entries.feature: A handle on the sampled process instance, not on a PID: ProcessHandles::acquire takes only a key from the live /proc source that names a process with a known PID, boot, PID namespace and LinuxBootTicks start time, in this boot and in the reader's own active PID namespace; it opens pidfd_open(pid, 0) and then re-reads /proc/<pid>/stat, whose start time must equal the key's, or the descriptor is closed and the acquisition refused (Replaced, Ended, Unverified); exit or PID reuse before acquisition and between the open and the re-check never yields a handle

entries.feature: A signal reaches only the handle's own process: ProcessHandles::settle sends one HandleSignal (Terminate, SIGTERM) through pidfd_send_signal on the held descriptor and closes it whatever the result; a process that exited after preparation answers Ended (ESRCH) and a replacement under its PID receives nothing; nothing is ever reopened or sent by PID; EPERM is Denied

entries.feature: Bounded handles: at most DEFAULT_MAX_LIVE_HANDLES (16) per table and DEFAULT_HANDLE_LIFETIME (30 s) each on a suspend-aware monotonic clock; closed on cancel, on expiry (expire, and before every acquisition and signal), on settlement and when the table is dropped; owned descriptors, counted closed by the fake and by /proc/self/fd on Linux

entries.feature: Unsupported and exhausted paths are explicit: not Linux, ENOSYS, EPERM/EACCES from pidfd_open (a filter or security module) and ENODEV are Unsupported, and ProcessHandles::probe reports it so the actions that need a handle stay disabled; EMFILE and ENFILE are DescriptorsExhausted, reported once and never retried; no PID-addressed fallback exists; minimum path Linux 5.3 (pidfd_send_signal 5.1) through syscall(2) with libc 0.2.189's call numbers, no glibc wrapper

entries.feature: PX-008's audit allows exactly the handle module's two system calls: only src/handle.rs may name unsafe, libc and syscall; libc:: only with one of six items, libc::syscall only with SYS_pidfd_open or SYS_pidfd_send_signal first, and unsafe only as one of three blocks pinned token for token; kill, extern and every other rule hold there; no other production file may name the module or its items; libc is an allowed normal dependency (already locked via srui-unix-security); DryRunExecutor stays the only production ProcessActions
